title: Interface-Engineered Flexible Conductive Metal–Organic Framework Films for Multimodal Energy Applications
abstract: Conspectus Conductive metal–organic frameworks (c-MOFs) represent a distinct class of porous conductive materials. Compared with conventional MOFs, c-MOFs integrate intrinsically high electrical conductivity with a high surface area and an ordered porous structure, enabling efficient electron and ion transport. Engineering c-MOFs into continuous and flexible films offers a promising strategy for translating their properties into practical devices. Key strategies for film engineering include solution processing, interfacial growth, and chemical vapor deposition, which allow precise control over the film morphology, thickness, and alignment of conductive channels. Thin-film fabrication preserves structural integrity and pore connectivity, enhances interfacial contact, and facilitates device integration, thereby promoting coupled ionic and electronic transport. These properties render c-MOF films suitable for multimodal energy transformation. In energy storage, their mechanical compliance, flexibility, and high porosity enable conformal integration with deformable and wearable devices while maintaining rapid charge transport and long-term cycling stability. In energy harvesting and conversion, their ordered porous networks, tunable electronic structures, and freestanding mechanically flexible architectures enable efficient adaptation to diverse energy inputs, facilitating energy conversion involving electrical, mechanical, chemical, thermal, and optical processes while maintaining the structural integrity under dynamic deformation. This versatility supports the development of integrated systems capable of simultaneously storing, harvesting, and converting multiple energy modalities for wearable and portable devices. This Account highlights our recent studies on the nanoengineering of c-MOFs on the surface of cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) through interfacial synthesis, enabling the fabrication of freestanding, flexible, and mechanically robust CNF@c-MOF nanopapers, as well as their applications in energy harvesting, conversion, and storage. We discuss the fundamental principles governing the interfacial growth of c-MOF nanostructures on flexible nanofibrous substrates, including the regulation of metal–ligand coordination and interfacial chemical interactions that govern hierarchical assembly toward functional flexible architectures. This Account also summarizes recent advances in the fabrication of flexible c-MOF films, covering representative preparation strategies, structural design approaches, and their unique roles in emerging energy technologies. Future progress in metal center selection, ligand electronic modulation, pore architecture optimization, interface engineering, and composite integration will further improve electron–ion transport, mechanical durability, and device-level compatibility. By combining flexible substrates with multiscale hierarchical structures, flexible c-MOF films can establish interconnected transport networks and adaptive functional interfaces, enabling high-performance, lightweight, and multifunctional energy devices. These advances highlight flexible c-MOF films as a promising platform for next-generation energy technologies that simultaneously demand mechanical flexibility, structural stability, and efficient synergistic electron–ion transport.

title: Tailoring Lead Iodide Crystals Through Organic Templating and Inorganic Heterostructuring for Optoelectronics
abstract: Metal-halide perovskites are leading candidates for next-generation solar cells and light-emitting diodes. Because the absorber or emitter forms by reaction of an inorganic scaffold with a cation salt, the crystallographic quality of the lead iodide (PbI2) precursor strongly influences device performance: small, disordered crystallites propagate grain boundaries, trap states and incomplete conversion. This article examines the structural chemistry linking PbI2 crystal engineering to optoelectronic outcomes. We contrast the electronic structure of halide and oxide perovskites and discuss how the A-site cation, rationalised through the Goldschmidt tolerance factor, determines whether three-dimensional or moisture-resistant two-dimensional phases form. Attention is given to template-assisted strategies, notably lead-fumarate and related metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) used as sacrificial scaffolds or interfacial buffers that promote large, oriented PbI2 crystallites and suppress halide-ion migration. We distinguish which degradation pathways such engineering can and cannot mitigate and assess its transferability to lead-free halides. We then present an original case study in which pressed PbI2/SnO2 composite plates (5 and 15 wt% SnO2), prepared by aqueous crystallisation, serve as a macroscopic model of heterojunction-mediated charge transport. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the PbI2 host retains its hexagonal structure in both composites. Under dark, daylight and 3–100 W UV (365 nm) illumination, the 15 wt% composite delivers roughly two orders of magnitude higher photocurrent than pristine PbI2, consistent with Type-II band-offset-driven electron extraction into a connected SnO2 network, while the diminishing gain per added wt% points to an optimum filler loading. These results provide device-independent support for the interfacial charge-separation principles discussed throughout.

title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal‐Organic Network for CO 2 Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous‐phase synthesis of a woven metal‐organic superstructure assembled from Cu 2+ and 2,4,6‐trinitrobenzene‐1,3,5‐triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu 2+ yields charged one‐dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two‐dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu 2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π‐conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox‐active Cu 2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu‐TNPG network was evaluated for visible‐light‐driven CO 2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu‐TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre‐activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H 2 , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

title: Functional Surface Self‐Assembly on Nitinol Biliary Stents for Enhanced Anti‐Fouling and Low‐Friction Behavior
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitinol (NiTi) stents are widely used for biliary decompression, but their biofluid‐exposed metallic surfaces remain susceptible to mechanical irritation, bacterial colonization, sludge deposition, and inflammation‐associated restenosis. Inspired by the dynamic, low‐adhesion interfacial function of the native glycocalyx, we developed a self‐assembled slippery liquid‐infused porous surface (SASLIPS) for NiTi biliary stents. The modified surface formed a continuous liquid‐infused architecture, exhibited water sliding angles <0.5°, and reduced adhesion under the tested conditions. SASLIPS decreased the coefficient of friction (COF) from 0.69 (NiTi) to 0.09 (SASLIPS), reduced biliary sludge accretion, inhibited 96.98% of E. coli adhesion and biofilm formation, and attenuated inflammatory responses, while preserving macroscopic thermally induced shape recovery. Molecular dynamics simulations supported favorable interactions between perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) and perfluorodecalin (PFD) and showed that the PFD‐rich interfacial region reduced water and cholesterol access to the modeled substrate. In a porcine study with independent 1‐ and 6‐month cohorts, SASLIPS‐coatedstents showed 89.92% lower sludge‐associated autofluorescence than bare NiTi stents at 1 month and no gross evidence of luminal obstruction at the 6‐month retrieval. This work established a liquid‐infused fluorinated surface strategy for engineering anti‐fouling, anti‐inflammatory, and mechanically compatible biliary stents, and offered a materials‐driven solution to persistent interfacial failure in biofluid‐rich implant environments.

title: Asymmetric Interfacial Stress-Driven Demulsification in Heterogeneous Wetting MOF Beds
abstract: Abstract Separating surfactant-stabilized dual-type oil/water emulsions remains challenging due to the intrinsic limitations of traditional single-wettability filters. Herein, a heterogeneous composite particle-based bed was constructed by blending pristine hydrophilic MOF UiO-66-NH2 with oleyl phosphate-modified hydrophobic MOF UiO-66-NH2–OP. The mixed bed combines droplet capture with interfacial destabilization: tortuous interparticle channels promote hydrodynamic deformation, while adjacent domains of contrasting wettability are proposed to induce asymmetric interfacial stresses and Marangoni-driven film disruption. Subsequent droplet coalescence and interception enable separation of both emulsion types. Filtration tests proved the composite bed outperformed single-wettability counterparts for dual-type emulsions, achieving over 90% rejection and a peak permeance of 5861.3 L·m–2·h–1·bar–1. This work establishes an emulsion separation strategy via MOF wettability modulation and particle-bed construction, shedding light on the design of high-performance, tunable separation materials.

title: Aligned Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
abstract: Abstract Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

title: Metal–Organic Framework Synthesis Strategies for Efficient Encapsulation and Sustained Release of Bioactive Compounds
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as versatile carriers for biomedical applications because of their tunable porosity, high surface area, and structural robustness. Their biocompatibility depends on carefully selecting nontoxic metals such as Fe, Zn, or Mg; safe organic ligands, including carboxylates, imidazolates, and pyridines; and stabilizing coatings such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), chitosan, and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) that enhance aqueous stability and enable controlled release. Conventional synthesis methods typically yield highly crystalline frameworks but require long reaction times and extensive solvent use. In contrast, nonconventional approaches are gaining popularity for their faster, energy‐efficient methods. Techniques such as microwave irradiation, sonochemical activation, and electrochemical synthesis provide rapid, controllable conditions that reduce energy consumption and shorten reaction times. In particular, mechanochemical encapsulation is an eco‐friendly, sustainable, scalable, and high‐yield methodology that enables in situ entrapment of bioactive molecules and enhances adsorption capacity. Moreover, the mechanochemical methodology enables modulation of physicochemical parameters such as morphology and particle size, which critically influence adsorption behavior and host–guest interactions. Examples of encapsulation processes involving antidiabetic agents, anticancer therapeutics, and antioxidants are presented, and these can be translated into mechanochemical approaches. In this regard, MOFs stand out as promising platforms for targeted delivery and sustained release. Integrating rational component selection, coating strategies, and sustainable synthesis methodologies positions MOFs as next‐generation biocompatible carriers for precision biomedical applications.

title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard‐Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion–Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard‐carbon anode design lacks a precursor‐level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed‐pore formation. Here we establish a precursor‐level cohesion‐solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene‐fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke‐like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard‐carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect‐engineered carbon galleries. The solvent‐selected AHC‐80‐1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide‐temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10‐kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC‐80‐1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg −1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle‐to‐gate life‐cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC‐80‐1400 production reduces climate‐change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor‐stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

title: Cluster‐Scale MoO x ‐IrO 2 Heterointerfaces Steer Dual‐Site Coupling and Interfacial Water Dynamics for Fast and Durable Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single‐phase IrO 2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass‐transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. Here, we design a Turing‐type MoO x ‐IrO 2 heterostructure with strongly coupled cluster‐scale interfaces, which enables dual‐function Ir‐Mo synergy that breaks fundamental kinetic limitations and optimizes interfacial water structures. At the reaction pathway level, Brønsted‐acidic MoO x clusters promote water dissociation to generate reactive Mo─OH* intermediates, triggering radical coupling with adjacent Ir─O* species to form OOH* and thus circumventing the linear scaling relation. At the interfacial microenvironment level, MoO x reorganizes the rigid hydrogen‐bonding networks and increases the population of free H 2 O species, effectively alleviating concentration overpotentials under high‐current‐density operation. When integrated into a practical 25 cm 2 membrane electrode assembly, this catalyst delivers a PEMWE cell voltage of 1.71 V at 3 A cm −2 and an ultralow degradation rate of ∼9.5 µV h −1 over 1000 h, with a total platinum‐group‐metal loading of merely 0.5 mg cm −2 across both electrodes. Our dual‐modulation strategy establishes a transformative paradigm for developing low‐iridium and durable OER electrocatalysts toward practical green hydrogen production.

title: Synergistic Interaction Engineering Enables Homogeneous Mixed‐Cation Perovskite Single Crystals for High‐Performance X‐Ray Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Mixed A‐site compositions are an effective route to boost the x‐ray detection performance of perovskite single crystals, yet their growth is often accompanied by pronounced spatial compositional inhomogeneity. This macroscopic phase segregation originates from mismatched formation energies and crystallization kinetics among the different cation components, leading to internal composition gradients that hinder carrier transport but are rarely addressed in perovskite single‐crystal research. Here, we report an acetic acid‐enabled synergistic interaction‐engineering strategy for growing phase‐homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals. Acetic acid simultaneously lowers the formation barrier of the formamidinium‐rich phase and suppresses the rapid assembly of the methylammonium‐rich phase, thereby balancing their crystallization rates and eliminating compositional gradients across the crystal. Owing to the improved uniformity and crystal quality, x‐ray detectors based on these single crystals deliver a sensitivity of 3.54 × 10 6 µC Gy −1 cm −2 , a low detection limit of 2.65 nGy s −1 , and excellent operational stability. This kinetic‐regulation concept offers a practical pathway to homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals and supports their use in low‐dose, high‐performance optoelectronic devices.

title: Membrane-induced eggshell biomineralization towards controllable crystallization
abstract: Abstract The avian eggshell is an extreme example of rapid biomineralization, yet how its underlying substrate, the eggshell membrane (ESM), initiates this process remains elusive, and the application potential of this fundamental biological mechanism has yet to be explored. Across the 33 avian species examined, ESMs consistently promoted CaCO3 crystallization under standardized in vitro conditions and exhibited low heterogeneous nucleation barriers. Inspired by this mechanism, we designed a biomimetic fibrous membrane (b-FM) that reproduces the structural and chemical features of natural ESMs. The b-FM achieves a deposition rate of 0.58 mg cm−2 day−1, surpassing the fastest natural ESM (0.46 mg cm−2 day−1). This efficiency arises from a threefold synergistic mechanism: (1) strong negative surface potential promoting Ca2⁺ accumulation, (2) reduced heterogeneous nucleation energy barrier, and (3) regulated crystallization pathways. Demonstrating its application potential, a b-FM/glass fiber mesh (b-FM/GF) composite module was employed for water softening in a circulating cooling-water system. In a 30-day continuous circulation experiment, the b-FM/GF-treated system maintained softened water quality and effectively suppressed pipe scaling, with less than 2% reduction in the effective pipe area. These findings reveal shared features of ESM-promoted mineralization and establish design principles for industrial crystallization control.

title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
abstract: Abstract Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

title: Elucidating Liquid‐Phase Guest Transport Across MOF Single Crystals: Interplay of Adsorption, Desorption, and Intracrystalline Diffusion
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide molecular selectivity in separations, understanding diffusion within these materials remains challenging due to the intertwined contributions of inherent pore architecture and grain boundaries in packed‐bed systems. To isolate the intracrystalline diffusion behavior, molecular transport across MOF single crystals was investigated in binary and ternary liquid‐phase systems. Diffusion rates were found to vary significantly even among guest molecules with identical kinetic diameters. By isolating the intracrystalline diffusion process, the slow transport is attributed to strong guest–framework interactions rather than pore clogging. This is corroborated by the increase in diffusion rates upon reducing the guest–framework interactions through selection of a more strongly interacting solvent. This study provides mechanistic insights into intrinsic diffusion in MOFs and benchmark behavior to calibrate computational approaches.

title: Dual-mode (light/dark) active nanocellulose–MOF–carbon dot filters for airborne bacterial suppression in hospital environments
abstract: Airborne microbial contamination in hospitals is a major driver of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). So far, most commercial air filters capture microorganisms but do not inactivate them, and they rely on non-biodegradable polymers. Here, we engineered bio-derived nanocellulose filters from oil palm empty fruit bunches and endowed them with dual-mode (light/dark) antimicrobial activity by integrating zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) and N/S-doped carbon dots immobilized on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (NS/CDs@MSN). Three-dimensional, highly porous scaffolds were fabricated via tert-butyl alcohol-assisted freeze-drying, yielding interconnected channels that promote airflow and contact between airborne bacteria and the active surface. Hospital air was sampled using a six-stage cascade impactor equipped with a cellulose filter, after that culture-based assays and MALDI-TOF/MS were used to characterize the trapped microorganisms. While pristine nanocellulose filters allowed survival of opportunistic pathogens, including Bacillus cereus, Bacillus thuringiensis and Staphylococcus epidermidis , the ZIF-8+NS-CDs@MSN composite filters achieved wide-ranging suppression of culturable airborne bacteria captured on the filter surface and within the filter matrix. Electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy confirmed the generation of multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS), including •OH, 1 O₂, and •O₂⁻, under both dark and 365 nm irradiation, supporting a dual-mode, ROS-driven inactivation mechanism that is synergistic with the presence of Zn-containing phases. Characterization via Nano-CT and XRF confirmed the uniform distribution of ZIF-8 and MSN within the 3D nanocellulose matrix, which optimized particulate capture and radical-pathogen contact. This study demonstrated a sustainable, ROS-active nanocellulose–MOF–carbon dot platform that bridges real-world hospital air monitoring and on-filter disinfection, offering a promising route to next-generation antimicrobial air-filtration materials for infection control in healthcare environments.

title: Length Scale Coordination Between Effective Electron Diffusion and Light‐Emitting Boosts Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemiluminescence (ECL), the emission of light excited by electrochemical reactions, has drawn attention as a powerful tool for bioassays and environmental monitoring. Nonetheless, a limited understanding of the bulk electron transport (ET) process in solid‐state ECL emitters, particularly the mismatch between the electron diffusion length ( L n ) at the photoelectrode and the light‐emitting layer thickness ( d ), significantly undermines the ECL efficiency ( Φ ECL ) and impedes practical applications. Herein, we report L n /d as a quantitative impedance‐derived kinetic‐matching descriptor of bulk electron transport in solid‐state ECL systems, and an empirical L n / d range (0.9–1.2) for achieving high ECL efficiency is identified from the slope behavior of temporal ECL evolution curves. This strategy was further confirmed experimentally across different ECL systems, including metal‐organic frameworks (MOF), poly(heptazine imide) (PHI), and carbon nitride with tunable band structures. The optimal L n / d ratio range enabled superior electron transport and mass transfer, yielding a record‐high cathodic ECL efficiency for carbon nitride (CN) and enabling a visual tetracycline (TC) sensor with an excellent detection range and limit.

title: EL-RAKHAWI ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL AND CONDUCTIVE INK FRAMEWORK (AFCIF) A Unified Paradigm for Printed Electronics, Bio-Fabrication, and Sustainable Smart Materials
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Advanced Functional and Conductive Ink Framework (AFCIF) redefines printing by transforming ink from a passive pigment into an active functional material across five integrated pillars: (1) Bio-inks with precise rheological control for 3D bioprinting of living tissues; (2) Structural color inks using nanophotonic self-assembly for fade-proof, pigment-free coloration; (3) Conductive inks for flexible E-textiles; (4) Smart IoT inks with stimuli-responsive properties; and (5) Circular deinking technologies. The framework's pinnacle is the El-Rakhawi Hybrid Synergistic Ink (EHSI), which resolves the conductivity-flexibility trade-off by synergistically combining 1D Silver Nanowires with 2D Graphene sheets, achieving >50% of bulk silver conductivity while withstanding >10,000 bending cycles. Mathematical rigor is ensured through the Herschel-Bulkley model for extrusion rheology, the Z-number criterion (1<Z<10) for inkjet stability, Percolation Theory explaining the lowered percolation threshold in hybrid networks, and the dimensionally consistent Frenkel equation for photonic curing kinetics. Integrating CNZF sustainability principles, QMRF mechano-quantum interfaces, and AQBI computational feedback, AFCIF establishes the material foundation for a circular, zero-waste electronics economy, democratizing manufacturing while preserving environmental harmony through dynamic covalent bonds enabling 100% ink delamination during recycling.

title: Thermo-responsive Ionizable Xanthone Bolaamphiphiles for Dynamic Self-Assembly into Nanovesicles Enabling Enhanced Intracellular Drug Release and Tumor Growth Inhibition
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive supramolecular nanocarriers capable of controlled drug release have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional chemotherapy; however, the development of structurally defined small-molecule systems exhibiting thermo-responsive behavior within biologically relevant temperature ranges remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of ionizable xanthone-based bolaamphiphiles (X1–X3) engineered to undergo temperature-triggered self-assembly in aqueous media. Systematic modulation of oxyethylene-chain density revealed that X3 exhibits a sharp and reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transition within the physiological temperature window (35–40 °C), leading to the formation of stable nanovesicular assemblies. The resulting X3 nanovesicles accommodate doxorubicin (DOX) with an encapsulation efficiency of ∼25% and a drug-loading content of 11% while maintaining good colloidal stability under physiologically relevant conditions. X3-DOX nanovesicles exhibit progressive thermoresponsive drug release near physiological temperature, which is further enhanced under mild hyperthermia, together with an additional acid-responsive release behavior associated with protonation of the piperazine units (apparent pKa ≈ 4.5). Cellular studies performed in 4T1 breast cancer and A549 lung cancer cells demonstrated enhanced intracellular drug accumulation, superior cytotoxicity, and effective suppression of multicellular tumor spheroids compared with free DOX. Furthermore, the nanoformulation exhibited excellent hemocompatibility, favorable biodistribution characteristics, and efficient systemic clearance. In a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model, X3-DOX induced remarkable tumor-growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. These findings establish thermo-responsive xanthone-based nanovesicles as a versatile supramolecular platform for controlled anticancer drug delivery and provide a molecularly defined strategy for developing stimuli-responsive nanomedicines.

title: Cisplatin Conjugated with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
abstract: Abstract Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large‐Area Tin‐based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin‐based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p‐type small molecule, 4,4'‐(5,6‐bis(2‐methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole‐4,7‐diyl)bis(2,5‐difluoro‐N,N‐bis(4‐methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic‐angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H‐ 1 H double‐quantum‐single‐quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning‐rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high‐quality Sn‐based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap‐assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG‐PEDOT:PSS‐based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1‐cm 2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04‐cm 2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N 2 atmosphere.

title: Pd Embedded in 1T‐Rich MoS 2 With Island‐Sea Confinement for C 2 ‐Selective Ethanol Electrooxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct ethanol fuel cells (DEFCs) are hampered by sluggish C─C bond cleavage and CO poisoning during ethanol electrooxidation on Pd catalysts. Selective oxidation to acetate through the C 2 pathway circumvents CO formation, yet achieving near‐exclusive C 2 selectivity remains challenging. Herein, we report a nitrogen‐doping‐induced expansion strategy that converts bulk 2H‐MoS 2 into a metastable 1T‐rich MoS 2‐x support (NTMS x ) with enlarged interlayer spacing and abundant sulfur vacancies. Conductive 1T domains preferentially anchor Pd nanoparticles, creating an “island‐sea” architecture that fosters pronounced electronic metal‐support interaction (EMSI). Electron transfer from NTMS x to Pd generates electron‐rich Pd sites that weaken CO adsorption, while sulfur vacancies enhance hydroxyl adsorption. These synergistic effects steer ethanol electrooxidation toward the C 2 ‐4e pathway and suppress CO formation. DFT calculations confirm favorable energetics for the C 2 pathway on Pd/NTMS x . The catalyst delivers a high current density and 95.7% Faradaic efficiency for acetate of high added value, with no detectable CO intermediates and outstanding durability. In DEFCs, it achieves a maximum power density of 0.68 W cm −2 and operates stably for over 500 h. This work establishes confined interfacial anchoring on phase‐engineered metal dichalcogenides as a rational design principle for achieving high pathway selectivity in multielectron electrocatalysis.

title: Laser-Induced Graphene Paper-Based Microfluidic Platform for Dual-Mode Electrochemical and Colorimetric Detection of Glucose
abstract: Abstract Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) provide an attractive platform for diagnostics owing to their low cost, passive fluid transport, and ease of fabrication. However, integrating dual-sensing capabilities into a single paper device while maintaining a simple manufacturing process remains challenging. Here, we present a foldable dual-mode microfluidic paper-based analytical device (DM-μPAD) that integrates laser-induced graphene (LIG)-based electrochemical sensing with enzyme-mediated colorimetric detection. A straightforward laser-patterning strategy was used to fabricate LIG electrodes directly patterned onto the polyimide tape-covered cellulose paper via a one-step laser engraving process, forming a conductive graphene network that serves as an electrochemical sensing module. A screen-printing process was used to form hydrophobic perfluoropolyether barriers, which define capillary-driven microfluidic channels that guide sample transport between sensing regions. The folded architecture enhances fluid-electrode interaction and enables simultaneous electrochemical and colorimetric measurements within a single analytical platform without electrode transfer or complex assembly. This dual-readout technique provides cross-validation of results to enhance detection reliability. The proposed DM-μPAD demonstrated good selectivity against common nonspecific compounds, a wide linear detection range of 0.01 to 3.0 mM, and a low detection limit of 9.23 μM in the electrochemical mode, while displaying a dynamic detection range of 0.1 to 2.0 mM with a detection limit of 57.9 μM in the colorimetric mode. Furthermore, the platform maintained high reproducibility, mechanical flexibility, and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of laser-induced graphene-based paper microfluidics as a versatile platform for developing portable, cost-effective, and multiplexed biosensing devices.

title: Reverse Micelles: The Gateway for Oral (Poly)Peptide Delivery
abstract: Reverse micelles (RM) have played a central role in biotechnology, yet their pharmaceutical use has been constrained by instability, high water content and non-biocompatible surfactants. Classical wet RM (wRM) contain a discrete aqueous core whose size and solubilization behavior are governed by surfactant packing, hydration level and physicochemical properties of the hydrophobic phase. Although these systems provided insights into nanoconfined environments, their sensitivity to dilution and environment has limited translation into drug delivery. Recent developments renew interest in dry RM (dRM), which reduce internal water to below 1% and rely mainly on interfacial rather than bulk-like water domains, with electrostatic and non-covalent interactions contributing to stabilization of highly hydrophilic (poly)peptides (pP). dRMs expand the application space for pP therapeutics, supporting delivery routes requiring low hydration and robust microenvironments. This review integrates RM architecture and outlines performance criteria for oral pP delivery, including high loading capacity, increased pP lipophilicity, protection from enzymatic degradation, enhanced epithelial permeation and favorable safety. In vivo studies demonstrate that dRM achieve comparable or improved oral bioavailability relative to hydrophobic ion pairs or wRM in selected systems, underscoring why RM remain relevant and why maintaining minimal hydration and formulation flexibility are central to unlocking their therapeutic potential.

title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
abstract: Abstract Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
abstract: Abstract Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La 0.2 Ca 0.7 Ti 0.95 Cu 0.05 O 3− δ , as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

title: Metal–Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores
abstract: Abstract Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2–96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4–99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

title: Chirality-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enantioselective Neuroprotection with Restored Neuroactive Signaling in Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation and a cascade of interconnected neurotoxic events, including oxidative stress, glutamate excitotoxicity, calcium dysregulation, and impaired neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling. To address the multifactorial nature of AD pathology, chiral d- or l-cysteine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) nanoparticles are developed as a multitarget nanotherapeutic platform. Both enantiomers effectively inhibit Aβ aggregation, scavenge reactive oxygen species, reduce extracellular glutamate levels, and attenuate calcium dysregulation. In parallel, d/l-Cys-COFs rescue compromised neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling, as evidenced by normalized expression of neuropeptide Y and brain-derived neurotrophic factor. In transgenic AD mice, d/l-Cys-COF treatment significantly improves memory and cognitive performance. Notably, the d-enantiomer affords superior neuroprotection through enhanced suppression of pathological intracellular calcium overload, whereas restoration of neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling remains chirality-independent. These findings identify chirality as a key design element for multitarget nanotherapeutics against AD, with enantioselective efficacy arising primarily from differential regulation of calcium dysregulation and shared restoration of neuroactive signaling contributing to the overall therapeutic benefit.

title: A Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework‐Based DNase I Delivery System for Targeted Suppression of the cGAS‐STING Pathway in Acute Lung Injury
abstract: ABSTRACT In sepsis‐induced acute lung injury (ALI), mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) released from damaged lung cells is recognized by the cytosolic DNA sensor cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS), leading to aberrant activation of the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway. This signaling cascade amplifies inflammation and oxidative stress, ultimately resulting in severe pulmonary dysfunction and high mortality. Here, we present a hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐101)‐based delivery system for DNase I that enables enzymatic clearance of cytosolic DNA and targeted suppression of the cGAS‐STING pathway in ALI. Following efficient pulmonary delivery and macrophage internalization, this DNase I@HOF‐101 platform effectively clears intracellular mtDNA, thereby attenuating inflammatory responses and alleviating acute lung injury. Moreover, the system exhibits desirable biocompatibility, minimal cytotoxicity, and enhanced enzymatic stability, highlighting its potential as a nanotherapeutic strategy for cGAS‐STING‐mediated inflammatory diseases.

title: Rational Construction of Defects in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Highly Selective Uranium Extraction
abstract: Abstract Through rational defect design, engineering covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to overcome the issues of insufficient active sites and poor selectivity is an effective strategy. In this study, we successfully constructed a molecular unit-induced defect-engineered COF using a stoichiometric control strategy for efficiently capturing radioactive uranium from rare earth tailings wastewater. The rational introduction of a molecular unit-induced defect can alter the charge density of the COF, thereby enhancing the adsorption performance of the synthesized materials. Especially, the synergistic effect of carboxyl functional groups and defects effectively reduces the hydrophobicity of COF materials, alters the adsorption environment of the pores, and enhances the selectivity for uranyl ions. Impressively, the tailored defect COF exhibits a remarkable uranium adsorption capacity (551.8 mg/g) under pH 6. Furthermore, the selectivity of the defect COF remains as high as 94.5%, and the Kd value can reach up to 6.1 × 104 mL/g under actual rare earth tailings wastewater. These results demonstrate that the rational construction of defect engineering can markedly enhance the efficiency and selectivity of uranium adsorption on COFs. This work demonstrates that the rational construction of defect engineering in COFs provides an effective route for enhanced uranium sequestration.

title: Super‐Toughness Self‐Healing Bimetallic MOF‐based Composite Solid Electrolyte with Nanoconfined Ion Channels and Dynamic Crosslinking for High‐Performance Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state lithium metal batteries are considered ideal candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to high energy density and safety. However, NCM811||Li battery systems face severe issues in practical application, such as interface failure between the cathode and anode, lithium dendrite growth, and the insufficient stability of conventional electrolytes. Here, we proposed a synergistic modification strategy combined with nanoconfined polymerization and interface dynamic crosslinking to fabricate self‐healing bimetallic MOF‐based composite solid electrolyte with enhanced ionic conduction and interface stability. The as‐prepared electrolyte exhibits high room‐temperature ionic conductivity (12.63×10 −4 S cm − 1 ), extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.14 V), excellent elongation at break (270%), high puncture resistance (5.28 N), superior thermal stability (200 °C), and outstanding cycling stability (94.77% retention over 150 cycles at 0.1 C), which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. Even under high mass loadings of 9.24 mg cm − 2 and 20.38 mg cm − 2 for the cathode, the capacity retention rates can still reach 90.88% and 86.35% after 150 and 100 cycles, respectively, demonstrating practical potential under high‐loading conditions. This strategy reconstructs the Li + transport, interface stability, and recyclability of composite solid electrolytes at the molecular level, paving the way for the development of next‐generation high‐performance solid‐state batteries.

title: From Nanoscale Interface to Macroscopic Conductivity: A Physics-Guided Graph Framework for Conductive Polymer Composites
abstract: Abstract The rational design of conductive polymer nanocomposites is hindered by an unresolved challenge: establishing a quantitative, predictive, and mechanistically interpretable link between nanoscale filler–polymer interactions and macroscopic electronic performance. Here, we present a physics-informed graph learning framework that integrates hybrid particle-field molecular dynamics with graph neural networks to decode this structure–property relationship in carbon nanotube (CNT)/triblock copolymer polystyrene-butadiene-styrene (SBS) systems. Through a physics-guided feature screening strategy, we identify the CNT/polystyrene (PS) interface as dominant structural descriptor for electrical conductivity, effectively filtering out polybutadiene (PB)-phase descriptors that are not directly relevant to conductivity. To overcome the limitations of purely data-driven models, we embed the classical percolation power law into a physics-informed graph convolutional network (PIGCN), enabling accurate predictions even in data-sparse regions near the percolation threshold at unseen concentrations. The convergence dynamics of key parameters (the prefactor η, percolation threshold fc, and exponent t) provide dynamic insights into network formation. Experimental validation on SBS/CNT composites with controlled aspect ratios confirms predictions: high-aspect-ratio CNTs establish long-range connectivity, whereas low-aspect-ratio fillers enhance network robustness. From these insights, we derive actionable design principles, including targeting the CNT/PS interface, leveraging aspect-ratio complementarity, and defining critical loading windows, establishing a knowledge-driven paradigm that bridges physics-constrained learning with experiment for the accelerated rational design of high-performance nanocomposites.

title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
abstract: Abstract Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
abstract: Abstract Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

title: Supramolecular nucleotide hydrogel as an artificial carbonic anhydrase for CO2 sequestration
abstract: Natural metalloenzymes achieve remarkable catalytic efficiency through precisely organized metal-ligand active sites within protein scaffolds, yet synthetically recreating this complexity remains challenging. Herein, we present a supramolecular strategy mimicking the architecture and function of a natural metalloenzyme in non-proteinaceous system. Exploiting the self-assembly of 5′-GMP into hierarchical supramolecular structures as a structural and functional analog of protein matrices, a tetrahedral Zn(His)3(H2O) center is spontaneously stabilized within an organized nanofibrous hydrogel. Experimental analyses combined with molecular simulations, demonstrate that nucleotide-directed supramolecular confinement cooperatively stabilizes the biomimetic Zn(His)3(H2O) coordination environment, creating an enzyme-like catalytic pocket. This minimalistic yet robust design, combining metal complexes with supramolecular assemblies, yields an artificial enzyme built solely from native biomolecules that closely resembles carbonic anhydrase II architecturally and functionally. The resulting ZnHG hydrogel exhibits efficient esterase and CO2 hydration activity with thermal stability and recyclability. CO2 hydration promotes biomineralization into diverse metal carbonates under aqueous conditions, establishing supramolecular nucleotide hydrogels as a protein-free platform for artificial enzymology. Natural metalloenzymes exhibit high catalytic efficiency, but replicating their complexity synthetically remains challenging. Here, the authors present a supramolecular artificial enzyme that mimics natural metalloenzymes and enables efficient, recyclable carbon dioxide hydration catalysis.

title: Effect of Ni(NO₃)₂ Precursor Concentration on Electrodeposited NiMn Electrocatalysts for HMF Oxidation to DFF
abstract: This study aims to develop a Ni–Mn bimetallic electrocatalyst for the selective oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF) via electrodeposition. The NiMn electrocatalyst was synthesized by varying precursor concentrations to tune its structural and electrochemical properties. The results show that an optimal concentration produces a highly crystalline NiMn structure with improved electrochemical performance. The optimized catalyst achieves 98.8% selectivity and 8.5% yield for DFF at 1.75 V vs. RHE over 6 hours, while simultaneously enabling hydrogen evolution at the cathode, demonstrating efficient biomass upgrading with value-added hydrogen production.

title: Limits of Knallgas bacteria for autotrophic CO₂ conversion: physiology, H₂ kinetics and reactor constraints
abstract: Aerobic hydrogen-oxidizing bacteria, commonly referred to as Knallgas bacteria, are chemoautotrophic microorganisms that oxidize molecular hydrogen (H₂) while fixing carbon dioxide (CO₂) into cellular material. Historically studied as model systems for lithoautotrophic metabolism, these organisms have regained attention due to their potential for renewable H₂ utilization, land-independent biomass production, and electrochemically coupled CO₂ conversion. Among them, Cupriavidus necator has emerged as a promising industrial platform, while thermophilic and high-affinity H₂-oxidizers such as Kyrpidia spormannii are increasingly explored in bioelectrochemical systems. Despite growing interest, substantial gaps remain between laboratory demonstrations and scalable industrial performance. This review analyzes the physiological characteristics of Knallgas bacteria, including growth kinetics and H₂ oxidation parameters, and evaluates their translation into gas fermentation and oxic microbial electrosynthesis systems. Particular emphasis is placed on key engineering limitations, including H₂ mass transfer, electron partitioning during aerobic metabolism, reactor safety constraints, and electrochemical surface scaling.

title: Supramolecular Aggregate-Functionalized Biomass Radiative Cooling Aerogel for Building Energy Conservation
abstract: Abstract Biomass aerogels have emerged as promising passive radiant cooling materials, offering a sustainable strategy for mitigating global warming. However, simultaneously achieving high solar reflectance, flame retardancy, and mechanical robustness remains challenging, substantially limiting their deployment in complex environments and long-term energy-saving applications. Here, we report a supramolecular aggregate-functionalized biomass aerogel (AMPx), which integrates effective radiative cooling, fire resistance, and mechanical stability. The aggregate is synthesized through supramolecular self-assembly reactions, using melamine (ME) and phytic acid (PA) as building blocks. By incorporating these aggregates into the sodium alginate matrix and utilizing directional freezing technology, the honeycomb-structured AMPx is prepared. The resulting aerogel exhibits a high solar reflectance of 92% and an atmospheric window emittance of 94%, enabling a temperature reduction of 11.4 °C relative to a commercial aerogel under direct sunlight. Building energy simulations further predict annual cooling-energy savings of up to 54.79%. Moreover, sufficient incorporation of ME-PA aggregates endows AMPx with rapid self-extinguishing properties. Interestingly, incorporating ME-PA aggregates increases the aerogel’s compressive strength and modulus to 3.71 and 12.17 MPa, respectively, representing increases of 334 and 168% compared with the original alginate aerogel. This work proposes a new paradigm for the development of functionally integrated biomass aerogels, demonstrating practical potential for sustainable energy-efficient thermal management.

title: Multidimensional biomimetic strategies for artificial bone scaffolds in bone defect repair
abstract: BackgroundCritical-sized bone defects remain a major challenge in orthopedic practice. Biomimetic scaffolds are designed to support bone regeneration by reproducing the structural and functional characteristics of native bone.ObjectiveTo synthesize advances in multidimensional biomimetic bone scaffolds, examine their roles in bone regeneration, and identify key barriers to clinical translation.MethodsThis narrative review drew primarily on literature identified through PubMed and Google Scholar, with an emphasis on publications from the past five years. Representative original studies and reviews were selected based on their relevance to biomimetic scaffold design, regenerative mechanisms, pathological bone defects, and fabrication technologies. Earlier publications were included where needed to provide foundational context. The selected literature was synthesized thematically across complementary aspects of scaffold design and application.ResultsThe synthesis integrates five interconnected design dimensions: composition, hierarchical structure, mechanical properties, biophysical signaling, and biological regulation. These dimensions link scaffold design to controlled drug delivery, reconstruction of a vascularized microenvironment, and neuro-osseous coupling. Preclinical studies report promising regenerative outcomes in models of infected, post-tumor-resection, and diabetic bone defects. Three-dimensional printing, electrospinning, and self-assembly offer complementary fabrication approaches for implementing these strategies across diverse material classes. However, limited clinical evidence and unresolved challenges in long-term biosafety, mechanical compatibility, functional stability, and reproducible, patient-specific manufacturing continue to hinder translation.ConclusionMultidimensional biomimetic design provides a framework for coordinating structural support with biological regulation during bone repair. Further progress requires validation of long-term safety and functional performance, alongside manufacturing approaches that balance functional complexity with clinical feasibility.
